title: Planning analytics — Norhaven Distributors
instructions: You are planning the Year 2 audit of **Norhaven Distributors**. Compute the ratios and identify the account and assertion each result most directly puts at risk. Use a 365-day year and round ratios to one decimal place (percentages to one decimal).

exhibits.title: Selected data
exhibits.content:
| | Year 2 | Year 1 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Net sales (all on credit) | 9,125,000 | 8,030,000 |
| Cost of sales | 5,840,000 | 5,621,000 |
| Accounts receivable, year-end | 1,500,000 | 880,000 |
| Inventory, year-end | 1,460,000 | 1,124,000 |
| Allowance for credit losses | 30,000 | 44,000 |

Industry gross margins were flat at about 30% in both years.

Interim work on the cost side is complete: the purchases cutoff, inventory costing, and the roll-forward from the physical count to cost of sales were all tested without exception.

rows.label: Days sales in inventory (Year 2, using year-end inventory)

parts.prompt: For each finding, select the account and assertion most at risk.

rows.label: Gross margin rose to 36% while the industry stayed at 30%
rows.explanation: An inflated margin suggests fictitious or early revenue. Understated cost of sales (completeness) would also raise the margin, but the clean purchases-cutoff, costing, and count-to-cost-of-sales testing rules that out, and receivables growing much faster than sales (DSO 40 → 60 days) points to revenue.

rows.label: The allowance fell from 5% to 2% of receivables while collections slowed
rows.explanation: A shrinking allowance on slower collections points to an understated allowance.

rows.label: Days in inventory rose from 73 to 91 days
rows.explanation: Slower-moving inventory raises obsolescence and write-down risk.
